Extracted summary:
- Props: variant="lea-watch", title="Key Distinction"
- Text: Key Distinction — The AoR is liable for DESIGN defects regardless of contractor performance. The AiCC is liable for CONSTRUCTION defects (solidary with contractor). These are distinct legal bases under Article 1723. One architect can serve as both AoR and AiCC, but the liabilities remain separate.
[/SLATECAMP_UI_BLOCK]

<LawCallout code="ra9266" section="Section 33 - Signing and Sealing">
Legal Basis: RA 9266 (Architecture Act of 2004), Section 20(a), which defines the Architect-of-Record (AoR) as the architect responsible for the total design, signing and sealing all architectural documents.
</LawCallout>

Extracted summary:
- Props: (none)
- Text: The AoR CANNOT delegate design responsibility to the AiCC. Design is NON-DELEGABLE. However, SUPERVISORY TASKS can be delegated. This line between design modification (AoR territory) and field interpretation (AiCC territory) is frequently tested on the LEA.
[/SLATECAMP_UI_BLOCK]
